name: Two Hands Shiraz Bella's Garden 2017
text:
## Two Hands Shiraz Bella's Garden 2017

**The story.** Two Hands was founded by Michael Twelftree and his partner Richard Mintz. Its Garden Series is a set of six Shirazes, each reflecting a different South Australian region, and each named after one of the founders' children; the vineyards are the "gardens" ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/a-decade-of-bellas-garden-47721)).

**The wine: Bella's Garden.** Bella's Garden is the Garden Series Shiraz from the [Barossa Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region). Wine Spectator, tasting ten vintages with Michael Twelftree, found it one of the series' standouts ([Wine Spectator](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/a-decade-of-bellas-garden-47721)).

**From the history books**
- **A misspelled valley.** Colonel [William Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Light) named the valley in 1837 after the [Battle of Barrosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Barrosa) in Spain, where he had fought in 1811; a clerical error registered it as "Barossa" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region)).
- **Three ships to Silesia.** In 1841 the South Australian Company chartered three ships to Silesia offering refuge and land to settlers; nearly 500 families came, and found the warm valley ideal for vines, though Silesia had almost no winemaking tradition ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region)).
- **From port to Shiraz.** For decades the Barossa made mainly fortified "port-style" wines, and in the mid-20th century it was seen as an inferior region, with its old Shiraz vines used in anonymous blends. In the 1980s, small family producers of old-vine Shiraz won international acclaim, and Jancis Robinson came to call the Barossa "Australia's quintessential wine region" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region)).
- **Protected by law.** To stop the valley turning into a suburb of [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide), South Australia passed the Character Preservation (Barossa Valley) Act in 2012 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barossa_Valley_wine_region)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) says 2017 began cool and wet, which brought disease pressure but none of the drought problems of recent years; the crop was plentiful, and dry weather through most of the harvest kept quality generally high.

**What the critics say for 2017.** As listed by [Nicks Wine Merchants](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2017-two-hands-bella-s-garden-shiraz):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 95**. "A real gem and well worth seeking out for readers who love high-class Barossa Shiraz": a kaleidoscope of red and black fruit, ground pepper, spice, herbes de Provence and cured meats; no hard edges, remarkable purity. "Impossible to resist today." Drink 2019 to 2029.
- **Nicks Wine Merchants: 97**, an Australian retailer's own score: blackberry, licorice, plum and black cherry, toasty cedar and dark chocolate; plush, with velvety yet structured tannins. Drink 2019 to 2027.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is nine years old. Dunnuck's window runs to 2029, so it is in its prime: drink over the next couple of years. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** Barbecued beef ribs, lamb with a spice rub, or the Barossa's smoked [mettwurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mettwurst).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Two Hands at the moment.

Sources:
- [Nicks Wine Merchants, 2017 Bella's Garden (critics' notes)](https://www.nicks.com.au/products/2017-two-hands-bella-s-garden-shiraz)
- [Wine Spectator, A Decade of Bella's Garden](https://www.winespectator.com/articles/a-decade-of-bellas-garden-47721)
